test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 26 May 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: After successive discounts of 25% and 10% a shirt was sold for ₹480. What was the original price of the shirt (Nearest to a ₹)?
solution:
Given:

Selling Price (M.P) = Rs. 480

Two successive Discount = 25% and 10%

Formula used:

Net Discount = (-X-Y+(XY)/(100))

S.P = M.P × ((100-D\%))/(100)

Calculations:

Net Discount = (-X-Y+(XY)/(100))

⇒ - 25 - 10 + 25 × (10)/(100)

⇒ - 35 + 2.5

⇒ - 32.5

Net discount% = 32.5 %

Selling Price(S.P) = Marked Price(M.P) × ((100-D\%))/(100)

⇒ 480 = Marked Price × ((100-32.5))/(100)

⇒ 480 = Marked Price × (67.5)/(100)

⇒ 480 = Marked Price × 0.675

⇒ Marked Price = (480)/(0.675)= 711.11 ≈ 711

∴ The original Price of the Shirt is Rs. 711.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Let the original price be Rs. 'x'

⇒ x × 75% × 90% = 480

⇒ (3x/4) × (9/10) = 480

**∴ x = (480 × 10 × 4)/ (9 × 3) = 711.11 ≈ 711.**
